title: Tensor sections describe change of topology for arbitrary scheme modules
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with Zariski site $T_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ of open subschemes [def-sc-zariski-site] and small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On the latter put $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}(u:V\to T)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. The inclusion of open subschemes induces a morphism of ringed sites [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] $\epsilon_T:(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})\to(T_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_T)$ whose module direct image is restriction: $(\epsilon_{T,*}G)(W)=G(W\hookrightarrow T)$ for each open $W\subseteq T$. For every sheaf $M$ of $\mathcal O_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], without any quasi-coherence hypothesis, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon_T^{-1}\mathcal O_T}\epsilon_T^{-1}M\ \simeq\ \big(u:V\to T\longmapsto\Gamma(V,u^*M)\big)^{\#}.$$
Here tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $u^*M$ is scheme module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and $\#$ is module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The presheaf restrictions are pullback of sections followed by the canonical composition isomorphisms, and its action on a module morphism $h$ is $\Gamma(V,u^*h)$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites], the inclusion defines $\epsilon_T$ with direct image restriction. The additive regular-functions sheaf [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction], after removing its universe lift, supplies gluing for $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$; ring operations glue sectionwise since restrictions preserve them. On an open $W$, its value is $\mathcal O_T(W)$, compatibly with restrictions and ring operations. The identity $\mathcal O_T\to\epsilon_*\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ has as adjoint the structural ring map $\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$; this gives the ringed morphism of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], whose induced module direct image is the displayed restriction with its ordinary $\mathcal O_T(W)$-action.

proof.text: Put $P_M(u)=\Gamma(V,u^*M)$. Semilinearity and the presheaf laws follow from [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]; [lem-sc-etale-tensor-sections-map-naturality] makes $P_h(u)=\Gamma(V,u^*h)$ natural. Set $L(M)=P_M^\#$ using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. These assertions apply to arbitrary modules.

proof.text: For $\theta:P_M\to G$, define $R(\theta)_W=\theta_{i_W}\Gamma(W,\kappa_W)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]. Its unit compatibility and the normalized restrictions [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] identify restrictions on opens with those of $M$; each $R(\theta)_W$ is $\mathcal O_T(W)$-linear since $\kappa_W$ and $\theta_{i_W}$ are. So $R(\theta):M\to\epsilon_*G$ is a module map, naturally in both variables. By [lem-trf-etale-tensor-sections-adjunction-extension], the explicit extension $\Theta(\beta)$ satisfies $R\Theta(\beta)=\beta$. Thus $R(\Theta R(\theta))=R(\theta)$; [lem-trf-etale-tensor-sections-open-determination] gives $\Theta R(\theta)=\theta$. Hence $R$ and $\Theta$ are natural inverse Hom bijections.

proof.text: The sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] converts these bijections into $L\dashv\epsilon_*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], applied to the ringed morphism of step 1, $Q(M)=\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_T}\epsilon^{-1}M$ is left adjoint to that same module direct image. Both adjunctions apply to all module sheaves, with no quasi-coherence. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with the identity comparison of right adjoints gives the unique unit-compatible natural isomorphism $Q\simeq L$. Step 2 specifies its tensor-section restrictions and action on module morphisms.
